title: Quotient of a Cohen–Macaulay local ring by a nonzerodivisor is Cohen–Macaulay
statement: Let $(S,\mathfrak m)$ be a Noetherian local ring [def-weil-pbc-noetherian-ring] of Krull dimension $d=\dim S$ [def-weil-pbc-krull-dimension-ring] (finite, as $S$ is Noetherian local), and assume that $S$ is Cohen–Macaulay in the sense that $\operatorname{depth}(S)\ge d$ [def-weil-pbc-depth], that is, $\mathfrak m$ contains an $S$-regular sequence [def-weil-pbc-regular-sequence] of length $d$. Let $x\in\mathfrak m$ be a nonzerodivisor on $S$. Then $S/xS$ is a Noetherian local ring of Krull dimension $\dim(S/xS)=d-1$, and it is Cohen–Macaulay in the same sense: $\operatorname{depth}(S/xS)\ge d-1$, i.e. the maximal ideal $\mathfrak m/xS$ of $S/xS$ contains an $S/xS$-regular sequence of length $d-1$.

source.place: Algebra, Lemma Tag 02JN (lemma-reformulate-CM, line 25319), last assertion with c = 1 ('each quotient R/(x_1,...,x_i) is a Cohen-Macaulay ring of dimension dim(R) - i'), the hypothesis that x_1 is a regular sequence being equivalent there to dim R/x_1R = dim R - 1; a special case of Proposition Tag 00N6 (proposition-CM-module, line 25052) and Lemma lemma-CM-one-g (line 25018)

proof.text:
($S/xS$ is a nonzero Noetherian local ring of dimension $d-1$.) Since $x\in\mathfrak m$, $xS\subseteq\mathfrak m
eq S$, so $S/xS
eq0$. The ideals of $S/xS$ are the images $J/xS$ of the ideals $J\supseteq xS$ of $S$, and the image of a finite generating set of $J$ generates $J/xS$; so $S/xS$ is Noetherian [def-weil-pbc-noetherian-ring]. Its maximal ideals are the $\mathfrak n/xS$ with $\mathfrak n$ a maximal ideal of $S$ containing $x$, so $\mathfrak m/xS$ is its only maximal ideal and $S/xS$ is local. Since $x\in\mathfrak m$ is a nonzerodivisor on $S$, [lem-weil-pbc-dimension-quotient-nonzerodivisor] gives $\dim(S/xS)+1=\dim S=d$ (Krull dimensions [def-weil-pbc-krull-dimension-ring]). As $S/xS
eq0$ has a prime ideal, $\dim(S/xS)\ge0$; hence $d\ge1$ and $\dim(S/xS)=d-1$.

source.place: Algebra, Lemma Tag 02JN (lemma-reformulate-CM, line 25319), last assertion, the dimension 'dim(R) - i' for i = 1; the dimension drop is Lemma Tag 00KW (lemma-one-equation, line 14694)

proof.text: (Supports.) View $S$ and $S/xS$ as finite $S$-modules [def-weil-finitely-generated-module], generated by the class of $1$, both nonzero (step 1). Their annihilators are $0$ and $xS$ (if $a\cdot\bar1=0$ in $S/xS$ then $a\in xS$, and $xS$ kills $S/xS$), so by [lem-weil-pbc-finite-module-support-annihilator] (localizations as in [def-weil-pbc-module-localization]) $\operatorname{Supp}(S)=V(0)=\operatorname{Spec}S$ and $\operatorname{Supp}(S/xS)=V(x)$, whence $\operatorname{Supp}(S)\cap V(x)=V(x)$. Here $\dim$ of a subset of $\operatorname{Spec}S$ is the supremum of the lengths of chains of primes lying in it, as in [lem-weil-pbc-cm-module-good-element-nonzerodivisor]. Thus $\dim\operatorname{Supp}(S)=\dim S=d$ [def-weil-pbc-krull-dimension-ring]; and since the prime ideals of $S$ containing $x$ correspond bijectively, preserving strict inclusions both ways, to the prime ideals of $S/xS$ ($\mathfrak p\mapsto\mathfrak p/xS$), the chains of primes in $V(x)$ are exactly the preimages of the chains of primes of $S/xS$, so $\dim(\operatorname{Supp}(S)\cap V(x))=\dim(S/xS)=d-1=\dim\operatorname{Supp}(S)-1$ (step 1).

source.place: Algebra, Proposition Tag 00N6 (proposition-CM-module, line 25052), proof, first paragraph (lines 25062-25068), for M = S and c = 1, which is how Lemma Tag 02JN (lemma-reformulate-CM, line 25319) proves its last assertion: 'Let Z = Supp(M)', and the chain Z ⊃ Z ∩ V(g_1), whose step decreases the dimension by exactly 1

proof.text: ($S$ is a Cohen–Macaulay module over itself.) $S\neq0$ is a finite $S$-module, so [lem-weil-pbc-depth-le-support-dimension] gives $\operatorname{depth}(S)\le\dim\operatorname{Supp}(S)=d$ (step 2), depth as in [def-weil-pbc-depth]. With the hypothesis $\operatorname{depth}(S)\ge d$ this gives $\operatorname{depth}(S)=\dim\operatorname{Supp}(S)=d$: the $S$-module $S$ is Cohen–Macaulay in the sense of [lem-weil-pbc-cm-module-good-element-nonzerodivisor] (Definition Tag 00N3).

source.place: Algebra, definition-local-ring-CM (line 25308: a Noetherian local ring is Cohen-Macaulay if it is Cohen-Macaulay as a module over itself), Definition Tag 00N3 (definition-CM, line 24960) and Lemma Tag 00LK (lemma-bound-depth, line 17813)

proof.text: ($S/xS$ is a Cohen–Macaulay $S$-module of depth $d-1$.) By steps 2 and 3, [lem-weil-pbc-cm-module-good-element-nonzerodivisor] applies to the Noetherian local ring $S$, the nonzero finite Cohen–Macaulay $S$-module $M=S$ and $g=x\in\mathfrak m$, since $\dim(\operatorname{Supp}(S)\cap V(x))=\dim\operatorname{Supp}(S)-1$. Its clause (b) says that $S/xS$ is a Cohen–Macaulay $S$-module with $\operatorname{depth}_{\mathfrak m}(S/xS)=\operatorname{depth}(S)-1=d-1$ (depth of $S/xS$ as an $S$-module, with respect to $\mathfrak m$). (Its clause (a) recovers that $x$ is a nonzerodivisor on $S$.)

source.place: Algebra, Proposition Tag 00N6 (proposition-CM-module, line 25052), proof, first paragraph (lines 25062-25068), for M = S and c = 1, which is how Lemma Tag 02JN (lemma-reformulate-CM, line 25319) proves its last assertion: 'Thus we may successively apply Lemma 00N5 (lemma-CM-one-g, line 25018) to the modules M/(g_1,...,g_i) and the element g_{i+1}', here i = 0

proof.text: (Depth over the ring $S/xS$.) Put $N=S/xS$ and $\bar S=S/xS$, with maximal ideal $\bar{\mathfrak m}=\mathfrak m/xS$ (step 1). Since $\mathfrak mN=\mathfrak m/xS\neq N$, case (1) of [def-weil-pbc-depth] applies to $\operatorname{depth}_{\mathfrak m}(N)=d-1$ (step 4), so there is an $N$-regular sequence $f_1,\dots,f_{d-1}$ in $\mathfrak m$ [def-weil-pbc-regular-sequence] ($N$ as an $S$-module; the empty sequence if $d=1$). Let $\bar f_i\in\bar{\mathfrak m}$ be the class of $f_i$. For $n\in N$ we have $f_in=\bar f_in$, so for each $i$ the submodule $(f_1,\dots,f_i)N$ equals $(\bar f_1,\dots,\bar f_i)N$, the quotients $N/(f_1,\dots,f_{i-1})N$ and $N/(\bar f_1,\dots,\bar f_{i-1})N$ are the same group, and $f_i$ and $\bar f_i$ act on it by the same map. So conditions (1) and (2) of [def-weil-pbc-regular-sequence] for $f_1,\dots,f_{d-1}$ on the $S$-module $N$ are literally those for $\bar f_1,\dots,\bar f_{d-1}$ on the $\bar S$-module $N=\bar S$: the sequence $\bar f_1,\dots,\bar f_{d-1}$ is an $\bar S$-regular sequence in $\bar{\mathfrak m}$ of length $d-1$. As $\bar{\mathfrak m}\bar S\neq\bar S$, case (1) of [def-weil-pbc-depth] gives $\operatorname{depth}(S/xS)=\operatorname{depth}_{\bar{\mathfrak m}}(\bar S)\ge d-1=\dim(S/xS)$ (step 1), which is the claim.

lean.statement: theorem depth_quotient_nonzerodivisor (S : Type u) [CommRing S] [IsNoetherianRing S] [IsLocalRing S] (d : ℕ) (hd : ringKrullDim S = (d : WithBot ℕ∞)) (hdepth : (d : ℕ∞) ≤ depth (R := S) S) (x : S) (hx : x ∈ maximalIdeal S) (hregular : x ∈ nonZeroDivisors S) : ∃ hQ : IsLocalRing (S ⧸ Ideal.span {x}), letI := hQ IsNoetherianRing (S ⧸ Ideal.span {x}) ∧ ringKrullDim (S ⧸ Ideal.span {x}) = ((d - 1 : ℕ) : WithBot ℕ∞) ∧ maximalIdeal (S ⧸ Ideal.span {x}) = (maximalIdeal S).map (Ideal.Quotient.mk (Ideal.span {x})) ∧ ((d - 1 : ℕ) : ℕ∞) ≤ depth (R := S ⧸ Ideal.span {x}) (S ⧸ Ideal.span {x}) ∧ ∃ rs : List (S ⧸ Ideal.span {x}), RingTheory.Sequence.IsRegular (S ⧸ Ideal.span {x}) rs ∧ (∀ y ∈ rs, y ∈ maximalIdeal (S ⧸ Ideal.span {x})) ∧ rs.length = d - 1
